expected_trigger: distributed (low and slow) credential stuffing: hundreds of IPs, hundreds of usernames, over an hour

alerts.reason: 32 distinct usernames failed from 28 sources in 3600 s (baseline 1.3, z=26.8)
alerts.observed_is: distinct usernames that failed in the window, from many sources (threshold: the learned baseline)

summary.summary: On 2026-01-23T14:51:00Z the auth-service recorded 32 distinct username login failures from 28 different sources within a one‑hour window, far exceeding its normal baseline of ~1.3 failures (z‑score 26.8). This spike indicates a credential‑stuffing event that is much larger than typical traffic. The incident was classified as HIGH severity.
summary.likely_trigger: A credential‑stuffing attack (ATT&CK T1110.004) causing many failed logins across many sources.
summary.suggested_next_check: Review the raw authentication logs for the affected hour to identify the source IPs and usernames, and verify rate‑limiting or lockout controls are active.
